text: TradeHQ exists to make financial education more accessible through practical learning. It is an educational simulator — not a brokerage, not an advisor.

text: Make financial literacy practical. TradeHQ lets learners place simulated market buys and sells, observe how orders and labelled practice prices affect portfolio value, and study the outcomes using virtual money.

text: A world where the first exposure to trading is educational, not expensive. Beginners should be able to make — and learn from — their first thousand mistakes on a simulator, not on their savings.

text: TradeHQ is a modern web application built with React, TypeScript and a serverless backend. Guest practice records stay in your browser so you can start without signing up. Account cash, positions and server-recorded trades restore across devices when available; earlier guest trade history and journals remain browser-held; signed-in lessons and beginner-journey progress can sync privately when online. The standalone mentor uses a built-in answer library and local topic matching without an AI API request; portfolio mentor tools can use simulated portfolio context.

text: TradeHQ uses AI-assisted drafting and editing for educational material and software. Checks include worked-example arithmetic, consistency with simulator features and source suitability within the scope recorded on each page. text: Community Reviews publish visitor-submitted feedback; we do not independently verify reviewers' identities or experiences. The Community Practice Board publishes optional, server-recorded ranked simulated portfolios, with earlier browser-reported results labelled separately. These are not independently verified investment results. Neither feedback nor practice rankings promise real-world returns. Educational figures use cited sources or clearly labelled hypothetical examples; when a question has no honest answer — which asset will rise, whether a strategy will work for you — the page says so instead of guessing. Content is revised whenever a reader points out an error or a market mechanism changes, and corrections are made in place rather than quietly removed.
